newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel votes to curb TV violence.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel votes to curb TV violence.

text.p: The Senate Commerce Committee voted Thursday to restrict broadcasts of violent television programmes unless the TV industry agrees to a content-based ratings system.

It approved a bill to limit violent programmes to times when children were not likely to watch unless broadcasters agree to provide more detailed information about shows so parents could decide if they wanted their children to watch.

The TV industry began a rating system this January based on age. Ratings include G for programmes that are suitable for everyone, TV14 for programmes that those younger than 14 should not watch and TVM for adult audiences.
"The American people know the age-based ratings system is a failure. It's time the industry understands it and moves towards a workable system," Sen. Ernest Hollings, D-South Carolina, said.
He said the V-chips to be installed in new television sets would not work without content-based ratings. V-chips allow parents to programme TV sets to block out certain channels.
The bill, approved 19-1, now goes to the full Senate. An identical bill has been introduced in the House.
